e48000007-web-14.title: Derbyshire resilience forum: Surface water flooding

E48000001-001.text: Water flooding normally dry land from rivers, the sea, heavy rainfall, rising groundwater or reservoirs, potentially damaging homes and services.

E48000001-002.text: Severe weather such as high winds, heavy rain, snow, thunderstorms, heatwaves or extreme cold that threatens health and disrupts daily life.

E48000001-003.text: Diseases spreading between animals. Some can also infect people, with consequences for animal welfare, farming and public health.

E48000001-004.text: Illnesses spreading through people, animals, contaminated surfaces or food, or contact with infected bodily fluids.

E48000001-005.text: Serious incidents on roads, railways, in the air or at sea, caused by collisions, mechanical failures or extreme weather.

E48000001-006.text: Accidents at industrial sites that can harm people or the environment beyond the site boundary, including chemical and nuclear facilities.

E48000001-007.text: Disruption to electricity, gas, water, communications, fuel or food supplies, with knock-on effects because essential services depend on one another.

E48000001-008.text: Deliberate threats including terrorism and organised crime, considered in local emergency planning even where sensitive details are not published.

E48000001-009.text: Crimes exploiting digital systems, including hacking, data theft and online fraud, which can cause financial loss and interrupt services.

E48000017-001.text: A complete failure of the national electricity network. Restarting power generation takes time, with knock-on disruption to essential services.

E48000017-002.text: An accident or technical fault causes a major winter gas shortage, affecting heating, cooking and people who depend on care.

E48000017-003.text: Prolonged snow, ice and low temperatures harm health and disrupt roads, schools and businesses. Frozen pipes can interrupt water and heating.

E48000017-004.text: A major tidal flood affects coastal communities across several counties, threatening life and requiring emergency resources to be shared.

E48000017-005.text: A new infectious virus spreads internationally, causing widespread illness and placing extra pressure on health services.

E48000017-006.text: Disruption to major roads, including the M20 and M2, diverts traffic onto local routes and obstructs port access and essential services.

E48000017-007.text: A port becomes unavailable because of infrastructure failure, severe weather, a security incident or sudden border closure, disrupting passenger and freight movements.

E48000017-008.text: A hazard such as flooding or a storm cuts mobile, landline and internet connections, affecting everyday communication and access to services.

E48000017-009.text: A regional electricity outage affects homes and businesses and disrupts other utilities, telecommunications and transport systems.

E48000017-010.text: Contamination introduces a disease-causing organism into food, causing illness and potentially requiring a lengthy investigation and response.

E48000017-011.text: High winds, extreme heat or heavy rainfall disrupt normal activities and can have serious effects on health.

E48000017-012.text: Rivers overflow or rainfall cannot drain away, flooding land and buildings and disrupting utilities and communities.

E48000017-013.text: Rivers rise rapidly after rainfall, potentially flooding nearby communities with little warning. The Bourne and Pent are local examples.

E48000017-014.text: A previously unknown or unusual respiratory infection spreads from an overseas outbreak and causes serious illness in the UK.

E48000017-015.text: Industrial action reduces the availability of emergency, health or care services. Action in supporting sectors can also affect delivery.

E48000017-016.text: Prolonged disruption at freight-checking sites, such as Sevington, interferes with the movement of goods through Kent.

E48000017-017.text: A major adult care provider stops operating and its services cannot readily be replaced, putting continuity of care at risk.

E48000017-018.text: A collision or other serious railway incident injures passengers or crew and requires an emergency response.

E48000017-019.text: A passenger vessel sinks in or near UK waters, requiring people to leave or abandon the ship.

E48000017-020.text: Oil or petroleum discharged from a ship harms marine life, coastal areas, tourism and other activities, with potentially lasting effects.

E48000017-021.text: A grounded or sunken vessel obstructs a major port, disrupting its passenger or freight operations.

E48000017-022.text: A tanker carrying dangerous goods crashes in a built-up area, causing fire or explosion, casualties, damage and road closures.

E48000017-023.text: A collision involving commercial aircraft causes casualties among passengers, crew and potentially people on the ground.

E48000017-024.text: An accident at a UK civil nuclear site releases radioactive material. The register identifies Dungeness as the local site considered.

E48000017-025.text: An accident at a nuclear facility overseas releases radioactive material that affects the UK or UK interests abroad.

E48000017-026.text: Fire or explosion at a site storing fuel, flammable liquids or toxic chemicals threatens nearby people and infrastructure.

E48000017-027.text: A reservoir or dam fails without warning, releasing fast-moving floodwater that threatens life and damages infrastructure.

E48000017-028.text: Piped water supplies stop, affecting households, businesses, agriculture and firefighting until alternative supplies or normal service are available.

E48000017-029.text: A serious building fire causes deaths or injuries, particularly where residents or patients may need assistance to evacuate.

E48000017-030.text: Fire spreads through forest or moorland, particularly during hot, dry weather.

E48000017-031.text: Volcanic ash reaches airspace used by UK flights, disrupting aviation according to wind conditions and the characteristics of the eruption.

E48000017-032.text: Repeated dry winters leave insufficient water to replenish supplies before summer, leading to prolonged shortages.

E48000017-033.text: Weather conditions trap or carry pollution over Kent, leaving unhealthy air in place until winds change.

E48000017-034.text: A highly infectious viral disease spreads among animals such as cattle, pigs, sheep and goats, with major economic consequences.

E48000017-035.text: A highly infectious bird flu outbreak causes severe disease in birds and can also spread to mammals, including humans.

E48000017-036.text: Rioting, looting, arson or other serious disorder damages property and harms community cohesion.

E48000017-037.text: Industrial action interrupts fuel deliveries, causing filling stations to run short. Increased demand can worsen shortages.

E48000017-038.text: An incident in a road tunnel causes casualties and disrupts routes that form part of Kent’s strategic road network.

E48000017-039.text: A sudden motorway or major-road incident closes routes during rescue, investigation and clean-up, disrupting local and cross-Channel traffic.

E48000017-040.text: Pollution enters rivers or underground water sources, threatening the waters on which Kent’s drinking supplies depend.

E48000017-041.text: Sewage, oil, farm chemicals or waste enter waterways and reach coastal or estuary environments.

E48000017-042.text: A building collapses, potentially trapping people and damaging neighbouring roads and utility services.

E48000017-043.text: A bridge closes or collapses, removing an important road, rail or pedestrian connection and disrupting the wider transport network.

E48000017-044.text: Equipment or process failure releases a large quantity of toxic chemical, potentially without a fire or explosion.

E48000017-045.text: Someone deliberately introduces a harmful chemical into food before it is sold or consumed.

E48000017-046.text: An attack makes critical transport computer systems unavailable, disrupting passenger journeys and freight movements.

E48000017-047.text: A cyberattack disrupts a major telecommunications provider, preventing broadband, landline or mobile communication and potentially access to emergency calls.

E48000017-048.text: A fuel business becomes insolvent, interrupting regional supplies for transport, aviation and heating while supply chains adjust.

E48000017-049.text: People are accidentally exposed to radioactive material that has been lost, stolen or transported without adequate precautions.

E48000017-050.text: A hazardous infectious organism escapes from a laboratory and spreads to people through close contact.

E48000017-051.text: Ground tremors or associated land movement damage the local area. The register treats such events as uncommon in Kent and Medway.

E48000017-052.text: Large numbers of British nationals return from abroad because of unrest or terrorism and require reception and support.

E48000010-001.text: Storms, snow, ice, extreme heat or drought can damage property, disrupt travel and utilities, and put vulnerable people at risk.

E48000010-002.text: Rivers overflow, rain overwhelms drainage, or the sea breaches defences, threatening homes, essential services and the environment.

E48000010-003.text: An infectious disease spreads widely, causing illness and staff shortages and putting health, care and other essential services under pressure.

E48000010-006.text: Gas, electricity or water supplies are interrupted, making everyday activities difficult and leaving some households needing additional support.

E48000010-007.text: Animal infections spread between livestock and sometimes to people, disrupting farming, rural businesses, tourism and supply chains.

E48000011-001.text: Coastal tides, overflowing rivers or overloaded drainage flood homes and infrastructure, with consequences for communities, businesses and essential services.

E48000011-002.text: Heavy rain, wind, snow, extreme temperatures or drought cause significant disruption to normal life.

E48000011-003.text: New flu strains or emerging infections spread between people, causing illness and potentially widespread disruption.

E48000011-005.text: An incident at an industrial site storing or processing dangerous substances can harm people or the environment beyond the site.

E48000011-006.text: Criminals or other hostile actors compromise digital information and computer systems, disrupting the services that depend on them.

E48000015-001.text: Infectious outbreaks, including flu, can seriously affect health, particularly among young and older people.

E48000015-002.text: Prolonged hot or cold conditions harm health and disrupt travel and everyday services.

E48000015-003.text: Accidents on busy roads, including those involving hazardous goods, can cause lengthy traffic disruption.

E48000015-004.text: Rivers, canals, reservoirs and other waterways can flood nearby homes, businesses and roads.

E48000015-005.text: Infrastructure failure or accidental damage interrupts electricity, gas, water or telecommunications, disrupting everyday routines.

W41000003-001.text: Coastal surges, overflowing rivers or other flooding threaten lives and damage homes, infrastructure and the local economy.

W41000003-004.text: A terrorist attack can cause casualties, fear and damage, with consequences extending beyond the immediate incident.

W41000003-005.text: Industrial explosions, fires or hazardous releases occur at sites or during transport, threatening people, property and the environment.

W41000003-006.text: Electricity, gas, water, communications or fuel services fail, affecting heating, food preparation and other essential activities.

W41000003-007.text: Contagious animal disease harms livestock, sometimes threatens people, and disrupts farming, the food chain and tourism.

W41000003-008.text: Oil, chemicals or smoke contaminate water, land or air, harming health, wildlife and local businesses.

W41000003-009.text: Accidents or severe weather disrupt important roads and other transport links, causing casualties, delays or isolation.

E48000004-001.text: Coastal, river and surface-water flooding can damage communities. The Dane and Bollin catchments can respond rapidly to heavy rainfall.

E48000004-002.text: Rain, wind, snow, ice and heatwaves can disrupt daily life, threaten health and interrupt transport.

E48000004-003.text: A new infection spreads between people across countries, putting health services under strain and disrupting work, education and essential services.

E48000004-004.text: Failure of essential networks such as power, water or communications can disrupt other services that depend on them.

E48000004-005.text: Attackers damage, disrupt or gain unauthorised access to computer systems or information, including by locking data and demanding payment.

E48000004-006.text: Accidents or severe weather disrupt roads, railways or other transport, potentially endangering people and delaying essential services.

E48000004-007.text: Accidents involving dangerous substances at industrial sites or pipelines can harm workers, nearby communities and the environment.

E48000004-008.text: Highly contagious or deadly animal infections threaten livestock, sometimes people, and Cheshire’s farming economy.

E48000004-009.text: Malicious violence, particularly at crowded or significant locations, can endanger people and disrupt communities.

E48000009-012.text: Rock and soil can fall suddenly from Dorset’s coastal cliffs, causing injuries and closing paths or routes. Wet and very dry weather can contribute.

E48000009-019.text: Strong winds and high waves damage buildings and infrastructure, interrupt power and transport, and can cause coastal flooding.

E48000009-005.text: Snow, ice and low temperatures make travel hazardous, harm health and interrupt electricity, water, schools and businesses.

E48000009-009.text: A new flu virus spreads readily through a population with little immunity, causing widespread illness beyond normal seasonal flu.

E48000009-017.text: Fire spreads through dry heathland or forest, threatening homes, wildlife and essential infrastructure. Human activity can start these fires.

E48000014-045.text: Strong winds and rain can bring down trees, damage buildings and interrupt travel and utility services.

E48000014-046.text: An extended spell of unusually hot weather can harm health and strain services, especially where people cannot keep cool.

E48000014-047.text: Cold temperatures, snow and ice increase illness and injury risks and can disrupt daily activities.

E48000014-048.text: High tides, storm surges and strong waves push seawater over coastal defences, flooding communities.

E48000014-049.text: Rivers, streams or brooks overflow their banks, often following intense rainfall, flooding surrounding land and buildings.

E48000014-050.text: Heavy rainfall exceeds drainage capacity and flows over land, sometimes causing sudden flooding far from rivers or the sea.

E48000014-072.text: The water table rises until underground water reaches the surface. Basements and cellars in chalk areas are particularly exposed.

E48000014-052.text: Pollutants build up in the air people breathe. Weather can trap pollution locally, worsening health effects.

E48000014-040.text: A large fire, whether accidental or deliberate, threatens people, property and infrastructure and can damage air quality.

E48000014-015.text: Trains collide with each other or an object, or derail, causing injuries and potentially major disruption.

E48000014-067.text: Chemicals or untreated sewage contaminate surface water or groundwater, damaging habitats and potentially interrupting drinking-water abstraction.
E48000014-067.section: Major pollution of surface waters and groundwater

E48000014-019.text: A road collision involving hazardous cargo can cause fire, explosion or contamination, threatening people and closing routes.

E48000014-025.text: The national network carrying electricity fails, cutting power across the country and disrupting water, communications, payments and other services.

E48000014-027.text: A technical fault or accident interrupts gas infrastructure, affecting essential services, industry and potentially electricity generation.

E48000014-024.text: Mobile phones, landlines and internet connections fail together, limiting everyday communication and potentially access to emergency services.
E48000014-024.section: Loss of fixed and mobile communications

E48000014-053.text: A new disease-causing organism spreads rapidly around the world through a population with little immunity.

E48000014-054.text: A new or newly recognised infectious disease causes an outbreak, potentially requiring enhanced detection, treatment and public-health measures.

E48000014-044.text: Solar particles and magnetic disturbances interfere with satellites, positioning, communications or electricity networks.

E48000014-042.text: An overseas volcano sends ash into the atmosphere, potentially disrupting flights serving the UK and Europe.

E48000014-051.text: A prolonged rainfall shortage leaves insufficient water for people, agriculture and the environment.

E48000014-069.text: Rock, soil or debris moves down a slope, damaging property or infrastructure and sometimes requiring evacuation. Coastal erosion and rainfall are local triggers.

E48000014-038.text: A water-supply interruption affects drinking, cooking, washing and sanitation, with additional consequences for vulnerable households and sensitive sites.

E48000014-011.text: A care provider suddenly stops operating, threatening continuity of support for people whose services may be difficult to replace.

E48000014-012.text: A private supplier closes or becomes insolvent, disrupting essential public services that depend on its work.

E48000014-016.text: A serious incident involving a ferry or cruise ship in busy local waters threatens passengers and requires a coordinated response.

E48000014-022.text: Damage or failure affects satellites used for communications, navigation and other essential services, with consequences reaching beyond the local area.

E48000014-023.text: Positioning, navigation and timing services are interrupted, affecting transport, communications, banking and other systems that depend on satellite signals.

E48000014-030.text: A bank’s technology fails, preventing customers from accessing accounts, withdrawing cash or paying for goods and services.

E48000014-032.text: An accident at a site holding large quantities of flammable or explosive material can endanger people and surrounding areas.
E48000014-032.section: Accident at a major hazard site

E48000014-035.text: Damage to a high-pressure gas pipeline releases gas, creating fire hazards, loud noise and damage to surrounding ground.

E48000014-039.text: Disease-causing organisms contaminate food through poor hygiene, storage or cross-contamination, causing illness.

E48000014-068.text: A serious collision closes a motorway or major road, causing casualties and wider disruption to nearby communities and businesses.

E48000014-076.text: Fire at a waste site releases harmful smoke or pollutants, damages property and disrupts waste services.
E48000014-076.section: Fire or pollution at a waste site

E48000014-077.text: A serious reactor fault on a visiting nuclear-powered vessel releases radioactive particles, potentially affecting the surrounding port area.
E48000014-077.section: Radioactive release by a nuclear-powered vessel

E48000014-060.text: Emerald ash borer beetles damage ash trees as larvae feed under the bark, threatening woodland, the environment and the economy.

E48000014-061.text: Large-scale disorder, including rioting, looting or arson, damages property, strains emergency services and harms community cohesion.

E48000014-062.text: A strike or other industrial action reduces public transport services and disrupts journeys.

E48000014-063.text: Industrial action by firefighters reduces the availability of fire and rescue services.

E48000014-065.text: Industrial action interrupts fuel supplies, affecting transport and services that depend on fuel.

E48000014-071.text: Industrial action by emergency-service workers reduces service availability and can affect urgent assistance.

E48000014-074.text: Strikes or action such as working strictly to contracted duties disrupt services or the supply of goods.

W41000002-001.text: Storms, prolonged snow, freezing temperatures or heatwaves disrupt travel and services, damage property and threaten health.

W41000002-002.text: River, coastal or surface-water flooding threatens people, homes and businesses, disrupts services and can isolate communities.

W41000002-003.text: Infections spread between people, causing local outbreaks or wider pandemics and placing pressure on health services and everyday activities.

W41000002-004.text: Essential networks fail without warning, affecting water, heating, communications, payments and other services.

W41000002-005.text: Industrial accidents, including fires involving hazardous cylinders in smaller workshops, can threaten nearby people and require evacuation.

W41000002-006.text: Animal disease harms livestock and can sometimes infect people; movement restrictions and losses affect farming and the wider rural economy.

W41000002-007.text: Accidents, severe weather, damaged bridges or tunnels, or industrial action interrupt transport and may leave people stranded.

W41000002-008.text: Rock, soil or debris moves down natural or human-made slopes, damaging buildings and services or blocking waterways.

W41000002-009.text: Terrorism, organised crime or cyberattacks target people, transport or infrastructure, threatening life and disrupting essential services.

W41000003-002.text: Storms, snow, ice or heatwaves harm health and disrupt transport, utilities, schools and other everyday activities.

W41000003-003.text: A new infectious disease spreads widely, causing illness and staff shortages that interrupt essential services and everyday life.

E48000031-001.text: A major adult care provider fails and suitable replacement services are difficult to arrange quickly.

E48000031-002.text: A company refining, importing, storing or distributing fuel becomes insolvent, interrupting supplies.

E48000031-003.text: A serious rail accident causes casualties, damage and possible evacuation or contamination.

E48000031-004.text: A tanker carrying dangerous goods crashes and catches fire or explodes.

E48000031-005.text: Two commercial aircraft collide in the air, causing a major emergency.

E48000031-006.text: A drone is deliberately flown near a major airport to create a safety threat and force airspace closure.

E48000031-007.text: A storm, flood or other hazard cuts mobile, landline and internet connections at the same time.

E48000031-008.text: The national electricity transmission system fails, causing a blackout across Great Britain.

E48000031-009.text: An accident or technical fault during winter causes a major interruption to gas supplies.

E48000031-010.text: An accident at a nuclear site abroad releases radioactive material with effects reaching the UK.

E48000031-011.text: People are exposed to radioactive sources that were lost, stolen or transported without proper precautions.

E48000031-012.text: Fire or explosion occurs at a site handling large amounts of flammable or explosive material.

E48000031-013.text: A large accidental release of toxic gas occurs at a hazardous industrial site, potentially without fire or explosion.

E48000031-014.text: High-pressure gas escaping from a pipeline ignites, causing fire or explosion.

E48000031-015.text: An infectious organism is accidentally released from a containment laboratory in an urban area.

E48000031-016.text: A reservoir or dam fails suddenly, causing rapid flooding with little warning.

E48000031-017.text: Piped water stops abruptly or becomes unsafe to drink, affecting households and essential services.

E48000031-018.text: A disease-causing organism contaminates the food supply, causing a public-health incident.

E48000031-019.text: A major building fire causes serious injuries or deaths, including in places where people need help to evacuate.

E48000031-020.text: An extensive wildfire burns for several days, requiring prolonged joint working by emergency responders.

E48000031-021.text: Volcanic ash intermittently closes parts of UK airspace, disrupting flights over an extended period.

E48000031-022.text: Strong ground shaking damages buildings and infrastructure.

E48000031-023.text: A severe solar disturbance interrupts electricity, satellite navigation, communications and aviation.

E48000031-024.text: Strong winds affect several regions, damaging property and disrupting services.

E48000031-025.text: Several consecutive days of extreme heat threaten health and disrupt everyday activities.

E48000031-026.text: Low temperatures and snow affect multiple regions, disrupting travel and services.

E48000031-027.text: Sustained heavy rainfall causes large river floods across several areas.

E48000031-028.text: Intense rainfall overwhelms drainage in a built-up area, flooding streets and properties.

E48000031-029.text: Several years of insufficient rainfall lead to water shortages.

E48000031-030.text: High concentrations of air pollution create an episode of unhealthy air.

E48000031-031.text: An infectious disease spreads widely through the population, causing substantial illness and demand for hospital care.

E48000031-032.text: A disease outbreak abroad reaches returning travellers and their close contacts in the UK.

E48000031-033.text: Infected animals are moved before illness is detected, spreading foot and mouth disease between farms.

E48000031-034.text: A severe bird flu strain reaches several poultry businesses through direct or indirect contact with wild birds.

E48000031-035.text: Midges spread a virus from an infected imported horse to other horses before the outbreak is recognised.

E48000031-036.text: African swine fever enters wild pigs and spreads to domestic or commercial herds before detection.

E48000031-037.text: Xylella bacteria infect plants and spread between nurseries or other premises through plant movements.

E48000031-038.text: Emerald ash borer beetles spread undetected through woodland and establish outbreaks at several sites.

E48000031-039.text: Serious public disorder occurs in one or more cities over several days.

E48000031-040.text: Industrial action by key rail staff brings large parts of the railway network to a halt.

E48000031-041.text: Firefighter industrial action reduces emergency response capacity over a prolonged period.

E48000031-042.text: Prison officer industrial action creates significant prison safety and security problems.

E48000031-043.text: Actual or threatened disruption to road fuel deliveries, including tanker-driver strikes, interrupts supplies.

E48000031-044.text: Vulnerable British nationals return from overseas without accommodation or support from family or friends.

E48000031-045.text: Major data-centre disruption causes outages across digital infrastructure used by government and public services.

E48000031-046.text: A faulty update disables widely used server software, causing a sudden digital outage across many services.

E48000031-047.text: The number of people entering prison exceeds available capacity, even after contingency arrangements are used.

E48000032-001.text: A new infection spreads worldwide, disrupting health services and everyday life.

E48000032-002.text: A newly recognised infection causes illness and requires enhanced public-health responses.

E48000032-003.text: Severe bird flu spreads among birds, sometimes infecting exposed people.

E48000032-004.text: Foot and mouth spreads between livestock, damaging farming and trade.

E48000032-005.text: Coastal or inland floods threaten homes, people, infrastructure and essential services.
E48000032-005.scope_note: Summary of local coastal and inland flooding guidance (PDF pages 20–23).

E48000032-006.text: Prolonged extreme heat harms health and disrupts services and routines.

E48000032-007.text: Cold temperatures and snow endanger health, travel and essential services.

E48000032-008.text: Strong winds damage buildings and networks and disrupt travel.

E48000032-009.text: Uncontrolled vegetation fires threaten people, wildlife, property and infrastructure.

E48000032-010.text: Shipping accidents release oil or hazardous cargo, contaminating the coastline.

E48000032-011.text: Accidents or severe weather interrupt roads, railways and aviation.

E48000032-012.text: Serious building fires cause casualties and may require evacuation.

E48000032-013.text: Essential networks fail, disrupting other services that depend on them.

E48000032-014.text: Supply faults, industrial action or protest interrupt fuel availability.

E48000032-015.text: Long-term climatic shifts increase extreme weather risks and alter water availability.

E48000032-016.text: Industrial fires, explosions or hazardous releases threaten people and the environment.

E48000032-017.text: Attackers steal, alter or destroy digital information and disrupt services.

E48000032-018.text: Deliberate attacks endanger people and threaten essential services and infrastructure.

E48000020-001.text: High tides and storm surges push seawater past coastal defences, potentially flooding communities rapidly with limited warning.

E48000020-002.text: Rivers overflow or heavy rainfall overwhelms drains, flooding nearby land and buildings.

E48000020-003.text: A new or increasingly common infection spreads through a population, potentially causing many people to become ill.

E48000020-007.text: A new disease spreads through people with little immunity, causing widespread illness and disruption.

E48000020-006.text: Gas or electricity supplies fail locally or more widely, interrupting services that depend on them.

E48000020-009.text: An extended spell of hot weather threatens health and can strain water supplies and other services.

E48000020-008.text: Prolonged freezing weather and snow endanger health, disrupt transport and interrupt utilities.

E48000020-005.text: Violence or threats intended to intimidate the public or influence government endanger people and disrupt communities.

E48000020-004.text: Criminals exploit digital systems to steal information or money, damage networks and interrupt services.

E48000034-009.text: Infections spread among wild or farmed animals, harming livestock and rural livelihoods; some can also infect people.

E48000034-005.text: Criminals exploit computer systems to steal data or money and interrupt essential services or business operations.

E48000034-003.text: Prolonged cold and snow threaten health, damage utility networks and disrupt travel, schools and services.

E48000034-002.text: Prolonged hot weather threatens health and may bring water shortages, wildfire and disruption to daily activities.

E48000034-008.text: Accidents at sites using dangerous substances, or major fires, threaten people, property and the environment.

E48000034-010.text: Deliberate violence threatens people and can target infrastructure, disrupting community life.

E48000034-004.text: A new disease spreads widely through people with little immunity, potentially causing prolonged waves of illness and disruption.

E48000034-001.text: Rivers overflow or heavy rainfall exceeds drainage capacity, flooding homes, roads and businesses.

E48000022-003.text: A new virus spreads quickly around the world where people lack immunity, causing widespread illness and disruption.

E48000022-002.text: Heavy rain, snow or strong winds damage property and interrupt transport, utilities and communications.

E48000022-006.text: Essential services such as power, water, fuel or communications are interrupted, affecting homes, businesses and daily life.

E48000024-001.text: Water from rivers, surface runoff, sewers or burst pipes damages homes and infrastructure and may require evacuation.

E48000013-001.text: Floodwater damages homes and businesses and interrupts daily life, with risks affected by rainfall and changing weather patterns.

E48000013-002.text: Storms, gales, snow or extreme temperatures damage property, threaten health and disrupt travel and essential services.

E48000013-003.text: A flu virus spreads worldwide through people with little immunity, causing widespread illness and pressure on health and care services.

E48000013-004.text: Accidents involving hazardous industrial substances threaten people and can contaminate the environment beyond the site.

E48000013-005.text: Accidents, infrastructure faults, severe weather or other emergencies interrupt roads, railways, trams and other transport services.

E48000013-006.text: Technical failures, emergencies or industrial action interrupt essential energy, water, food, communication, health or financial services.

E48000025-001.text: Flooding damages communities and disrupts everyday life; surface-water flooding can develop with very little warning.

E48000025-002.text: Heat, cold, snow, strong winds or extreme rainfall disrupt travel, threaten health and affect communities.

E48000025-003.text: A new flu virus spreads rapidly through people with little immunity, causing more widespread illness than ordinary seasonal flu.

E48000025-004.text: An accident involving dangerous industrial chemicals threatens people and the environment.

E48000025-007.text: Animal disease threatens livestock, food production, wildlife and farming livelihoods, and some infections can also affect people.

E48000035-002.text: Criminals use digital systems to steal information or money, promote a cause or prevent services from working.

E48000035-003.text: Organised criminals exploit people and businesses through activities such as trafficking, drugs, firearms, fraud and cybercrime.

E48000035-004.text: Industrial accidents, hazardous-material releases or failures of utility networks disrupt services and threaten people or the environment.

E48000035-005.text: Extreme weather and flooding threaten communities, damage property and interrupt everyday services.

E48000035-007.text: Disorder or industrial action damages communities or reduces essential services, including transport, health and education.

E48000035-006.text: Human infections can spread widely, while animal diseases threaten health, food production and rural livelihoods.
E48000035-006.scope_note: Summary of the local human and animal disease guidance (PDF pages 20–21).

E48000027-001.text: Flooding endangers people, damages homes and businesses and can interrupt roads, utilities and public services for a long time.

E48000027-003.text: A new infectious organism spreads through the population, affecting health and disrupting daily life and services.

E48000027-004.text: Electricity, gas, water or communications fail, sometimes without warning, with knock-on effects on other essential services.

E48000027-005.text: Industrial accidents can escalate rapidly, threatening people and requiring a coordinated emergency response.

E48000027-006.text: Road, railway or aviation incidents cause casualties and disruption; vehicle fires or hazardous loads can increase the consequences.

W41000004-001.text: Infections spread through communities, causing illness and disrupting schools, workplaces and health services.

W41000004-002.text: An epidemic spreads across countries or a very large area, affecting many people. The term describes spread, not necessarily severity.

W41000004-003.text: Storms, gales, snow, cold, heatwaves or drought threaten health, damage property and disrupt transport and communications.

W41000004-004.text: Floodwater from rivers, the sea, groundwater, surface runoff or reservoirs threatens homes and services and can isolate communities.

W41000004-005.text: Rock, earth or debris moves suddenly or slowly, threatening life and infrastructure. Disused coal tips on steep hillsides are a particular local concern.

W41000004-006.text: Explosions, fires or hazardous releases at industrial sites or during transport threaten people and the environment.

W41000004-007.text: Power, water, gas, fuel or communications are interrupted, affecting sanitation, heating, payments and essential services.

W41000004-008.text: Contagious animal disease harms livestock and farming livelihoods, and some infections can spread to people.

W41000004-009.text: Terrorism, organised crime or cyberattacks threaten people, crowded places, transport and essential infrastructure.

E48000019-001.text: Rivers overflow or heavy rain overwhelms drainage, flooding homes, businesses and roads.

E48000019-002.text: Heatwaves, drought, freezing conditions, snow, storms or heavy rain threaten health and disrupt daily life.

E48000019-003.text: Faults, deliberate attacks or industrial action interrupt gas, electricity or water supplies, locally or over a wide area.

E48000019-004.text: Infectious diseases cause local outbreaks or wider pandemics, with consequences for health, care and everyday services.

E48000019-005.text: Malicious digital activity steals personal or business information, causes financial losses and disrupts services.

E48000019-006.text: Serious incidents on busy road, rail or air routes threaten people and disrupt travel and the movement of goods.

E48000019-007.text: A deliberate attack causes physical harm, psychological trauma, property damage and disruption to communities.

E48000012-001.text: Infectious outbreaks or pandemics threaten health and can seriously disrupt the economy and social wellbeing.

E48000012-002.text: A deliberate violent attack threatens lives and public safety, requiring a coordinated emergency response.

E48000012-003.text: National, regional or local power supplies fail; damage to network equipment can leave some areas disconnected for an extended period.

E48000012-004.text: River flooding or heavy rain overwhelming drainage damages property and causes disruption and lasting effects on wellbeing.

E48000012-005.text: Fuel shortages, infrastructure faults, industrial action or protest interrupt supplies for transport and essential services.

E48000012-006.text: Snow, strong winds, heatwaves or heavy rainfall threaten people and disrupt services; climate change can worsen some extremes.

E48000012-007.text: Cybercrime targets accounts, data and devices, harming individuals and businesses and interrupting essential services.

E48000028-001.text: Heavy rainfall raises rivers beyond their capacity, flooding homes and transport routes and potentially requiring evacuation.

E48000028-002.text: Storms, snow or ice damage property, threaten health and interrupt roads, utilities and essential services.

E48000028-003.text: Infections spread between people and can become widespread epidemics or pandemics, putting pressure on care and disrupting work and services.

E48000016-001.text: Flooding from rivers, the coast or surface water threatens homes, businesses, services and the environment.

E48000016-003.text: A flu pandemic spreads illness widely, affecting health services and daily activities across the population.

E48000016-004.text: A new infectious disease spreads among people, requiring public-health action to contain its effects.

E48000016-005.text: Industrial activities involving hazardous substances can cause fires or releases that harm people and the environment.

E48000016-007.text: Electricity supplies fail, disrupting daily life and other utilities and services that depend on power.

E48000016-008.text: Animal infections such as foot and mouth or bird flu threaten farming and can harm livelihoods and trade.

E48000016-002.text: Cold, snow and storms disrupt travel and utilities, while heatwaves and drought threaten health and water supplies.
E48000016-002.scope_note: Summary of local cold-weather and heatwave guidance (PDF pages 8 and 12).

E48000006-001.text: Rivers and watercourses flood surrounding land; these events can coincide with coastal, surface-water or flash flooding.

E48000006-003.text: A new disease spreads rapidly around the world, potentially causing repeated waves of illness.

E48000029-043.text: Prolonged or heavy rainfall causes rivers and waterways to overflow, damaging property and interrupting roads and services.

E48000029-034.text: A serious building fire threatens people and can close roads or disrupt the surrounding area for a long time.

E48000029-042.text: Snow and ice block routes and isolate communities, while cold temperatures threaten health and interrupt power supplies.

E48000029-046.text: A new infection spreads quickly worldwide, causing widespread illness and pressure on health, schools and other services.

E48000029-041.text: Several days of unusually hot weather threaten health and can strain water, electricity and transport services.

E48000029-049.text: Bird flu spreads through wild birds and poultry, requiring controls to protect flocks and limit further spread.

E48000029-028.text: An accidental fire or explosion at a chemical site threatens the surrounding area.

E48000029-029.text: An accidental chemical leak at an industrial site affects the surrounding area.

E48000029-031.text: A reservoir or dam fails, releasing a large volume of water rapidly and causing severe flooding.

E48000029-040.text: Strong winds damage buildings, bring down trees and interrupt power and travel.

E48000029-045.text: Pollutants build up in the air, particularly during still or hot weather, threatening health.

E48000029-044.text: A long period of low rainfall reduces water availability for homes, farming and the environment.

E48000029-022.text: A fault, severe weather or pipe damage interrupts gas supplies, affecting heating, hot water and cooking.

E48000029-019.text: Damage to phone lines, mobile masts or internet cables interrupts communications, online services and card payments.

E48000029-033.text: Food is contaminated accidentally or deliberately and becomes unsafe to eat.

E48000036-001.text: An accident involving dangerous industrial substances causes injuries or harms the surrounding area.

E48000036-002.text: Electricity supplies stop, affecting lighting, appliances and digital landlines until power is restored.

E48000036-003.text: Heatwaves, cold, snow, flooding or strong winds threaten people and interrupt everyday activities.

E48000036-006.text: Excessive heat threatens health, particularly for young, older or medically vulnerable people.

E48000036-007.text: Very cold conditions increase the risk of illness and injury, with some people needing extra support.

E48000036-008.text: Disorder or industrial action damages communities or reduces essential services and business activity.

E48000036-009.text: A disease spreads widely in a short time, causing widespread illness and pressure on services.
E48000036-009.scope_note: The local health-emergencies section describes pandemic illness.

E48000036-010.text: Accidents, severe weather, flooding or strikes interrupt transport networks and delay journeys and deliveries.

E48000036-011.text: A malicious attempt damages or disrupts a computer network or system.

E48000036-012.text: Fuel deliveries are disrupted and supplies run short; extra buying can make shortages worse.

E48000036-013.text: A deliberate attack threatens public safety and may happen with little warning.

E48000033-011.text: Cold, snow and ice make journeys hazardous, close schools and interrupt transport and utilities.

E48000033-010.text: Very high temperatures threaten health, especially for people who are older, very young or have existing health conditions.

E48000033-013.text: An infection spreads widely across countries, causing illness and disruption to daily life and essential services.

E48000005-001.text: Flooding from the sea, rivers, drainage or dam failure threatens life, damages property and disrupts communities.

E48000005-002.text: Winter weather and prolonged heat threaten health and disrupt travel, utilities, schools and care services.
E48000005-002.scope_note: Summary of local winter-weather and heatwave guidance (PDF pages 11–12).

E48000005-005.text: A new infectious organism spreads readily between people, causing widespread illness and pressure on care and other essential services.

E48000005-006.text: Animal infections spread between livestock and sometimes to people, damaging rural economies, tourism and food-related businesses.

E48000005-007.text: Electricity, gas or water supplies are interrupted, making daily activities difficult until services are restored.

E48000011-004.text: Disease spreads among animals and can sometimes infect people. Outbreak controls can restrict livestock movements and disrupt farming.

E48000011-007.text: Electricity, gas or water supplies fail, affecting daily life and creating additional difficulties for vulnerable households.

E48000038-002.text: River, groundwater or surface-water flooding damages homes and businesses; the Avon and the Salisbury area have notable local exposure.

E48000038-001.text: A new infectious disease spreads internationally, causing widespread illness and disruption to society.

E48000026-001.text: Flooding threatens life, damages homes and infrastructure, displaces residents and can have lasting effects on health and the local economy.

E48000026-002.text: Strong winds, cold or heat harm health, damage property and utility equipment, and disrupt travel.

E48000026-003.text: Gas, electricity or water supplies fail, disrupting daily activities and creating extra difficulties for vulnerable households.

E48000026-004.text: A new flu strain spreads readily between people with little immunity, causing illness, staff shortages and pressure on care services.

E48000026-005.text: An incident at a site processing or storing dangerous substances harms nearby people, property or the environment.

E48000026-007.text: Infections spread among animals and sometimes to people, harming rural communities, farming and tourism.

E48000037-001.text: Flooding damages homes and infrastructure, isolates communities and interrupts transport and utilities, sometimes with little warning.

E48000037-002.text: Cold, snow, storms or extreme heat threaten health, damage infrastructure and interrupt businesses and travel.

E48000037-003.text: An infection spreads readily between people, causing widespread illness, staff shortages and pressure on health and care services.
E48000037-003.scope_note: The local register’s health guidance focuses on pandemic disease.

E48000037-007.text: A deliberate attack causes casualties or damage and disrupts infrastructure and essential services.

E48000007-001.text: Rivers such as the Derwent, Dove, Rother and Trent overflow their floodplains, threatening nearby property even where defences exist.

E48000007-002.text: Heavy rain runs off land and roads or overwhelms drainage, causing sudden flooding away from main river floodplains.

E48000007-003.text: Prolonged freezing, deep snow, heatwaves, gales or storms threaten normal activities and can cause widespread disruption.

E48000007-009.text: Accidents involving hazardous substances in storage, processing or transport can cause casualties and pollution beyond the immediate site.

E48000030-001.text: Coastal, river or surface-water flooding threatens communities and businesses, damages infrastructure and can have lasting effects on health.

E48000030-002.text: Heavy rainfall, snow or extreme heat disrupt everyday activities and require coordinated preparations and response.

NRR26-001.text: A terrorist attack overseas that affects British nationals, potentially causing deaths, injuries and a need for support or repatriation.

NRR26-002.text: Terrorist violence linked to Northern Ireland, including attempts to destabilise the peace settlement and harm people or public services.

NRR26-003.text: An attack using an explosive device carried by a person, placed at a location, or transported in a vehicle.

NRR26-004.text: An attack in which perpetrators move through an area seeking victims, using methods such as vehicles, knives or firearms.

NRR26-005.text: A deliberate attack affecting ships, ports or other maritime activity, with potential harm to people and disruption to transport.

NRR26-006.text: A deliberate attack on the rail network or its passengers, potentially causing casualties and interrupting rail services.

NRR26-007.text: An attack on aircraft or aviation infrastructure intended to cause harm and disruption to air travel.

NRR26-008.text: An incident in which people are held or threatened to force demands, potentially for political or ideological purposes.

NRR26-009.text: The deliberate killing or attempted killing of a prominent public figure.

NRR26-010.text: An attack using chemical, biological, radioactive or nuclear material to harm people, contaminate an area or disrupt services.

NRR26-011.text: A physical attack on gas infrastructure that interrupts operations or supplies and may endanger people nearby.

NRR26-012.text: A cyber attack that damages or disrupts the digital systems used to operate gas infrastructure.

NRR26-013.text: A physical attack on electricity infrastructure, potentially damaging equipment and interrupting power supplies.

NRR26-014.text: A cyber attack on electricity systems that could disrupt the transmission network and cause a widespread power outage.

NRR26-015.text: A physical attack on a civil nuclear facility or related infrastructure, with potential consequences for safety and energy supplies.

NRR26-016.text: A physical attack on facilities used to produce, import, store or distribute fuel, potentially interrupting supplies and harming workers.

NRR26-017.text: A cyber attack that interrupts the production or distribution of fuel by disrupting the systems used by fuel suppliers.

NRR26-018.text: A physical attack on a government building or estate that threatens people, assets or the continuity of government services.

NRR26-019.text: A cyber attack on health or social care systems that interrupts services, compromises information or limits access to essential systems.

NRR26-020.text: A cyber attack on transport networks or operating systems that disrupts travel and the movement of people or goods.

NRR26-021.text: A cyber attack on systems supporting fixed-line, mobile or internet communications, potentially disrupting essential connections.

NRR26-022.text: A cyber attack on data centres or the infrastructure supporting digital services used by businesses, public services and individuals.

NRR26-023.text: A cyber attack on digital systems controlling water treatment or distribution that could interrupt water supplies or wastewater services.

NRR26-024.text: A cyber attack on policing systems that could interrupt police operations and the delivery of emergency services.

NRR26-025.text: Malicious interference with civil nuclear systems, including digital systems, that threatens safe operations or essential services.

NRR26-026.text: A malicious attack on financial infrastructure that supports transactions essential to the UK economy.

NRR26-027.text: A malicious attack on a retail bank that could prevent customers from accessing accounts, payments or other banking services.

NRR26-028.text: Major disruption to the undersea telecommunications cables carrying international internet and data traffic to and from the UK.

NRR26-029.text: Disruption of international routes used to transport oil, potentially affecting supplies, energy prices, production and wider trade.

NRR26-030.text: Interference intended to undermine or disrupt democratic processes in the UK, including the integrity of elections and public participation.

NRR26-031.text: The failure of a major adult social care provider, putting the continuity of care for people with support needs at risk.

NRR26-032.text: The insolvency of a major supplier whose failure could interrupt services essential to the public sector.

NRR26-033.text: The insolvency of a fuel-sector business, potentially disrupting the supply of fuel while its operations are closed, sold or transferred.

NRR26-034.text: A serious rail accident, such as a derailment, that could cause injuries, damage and disruption to train services.

NRR26-035.text: A major accident involving a large passenger vessel, such as a cruise ship, potentially requiring rescue and emergency support.

NRR26-036.text: A major release of pollutants into UK waters, for example oil spilled from a tanker, pipeline or offshore installation.

NRR26-037.text: A vessel accident that obstructs a major UK port and interrupts the movement of imports and exports.

NRR26-038.text: An accident involving dangerous materials whose release could seriously harm people, public safety or the environment.

NRR26-039.text: A serious aircraft collision, with potential loss of life, injuries and disruption to aviation.

NRR26-040.text: Malicious use of a drone that threatens safety or disrupts operations, including activity around an airport.

NRR26-041.text: The loss or degradation of satellite communications, remote sensing or other space-based services that support activities on Earth.

NRR26-042.text: The loss of positioning, navigation or precise timing services used by transport, communications and other critical systems.

NRR26-043.text: A simultaneous loss of fixed and mobile communications, potentially disrupting broadband, telephone connections and access to essential services.

NRR26-044.text: A failure of the national electricity transmission system causing widespread loss of power and disruption across other essential systems.

NRR26-045.text: Failure of part of the electricity distribution network, causing a power outage across a region rather than the whole country.

NRR26-046.text: A shortage of gas or electricity relative to national demand, requiring action to manage supplies and protect essential services.

NRR26-047.text: An accident involving civil nuclear facilities or activities that could release radiation and require measures to protect the public.

NRR26-048.text: A radioactive release from a nuclear facility outside the UK, with potential consequences for people or the environment in the UK.

NRR26-049.text: Exposure to radioactive material while goods are being transported, or after a radioactive source has been lost or stolen.

NRR26-050.text: A technological failure at a major retail bank that interrupts customers’ access to accounts, payments or banking services.

NRR26-051.text: A technological failure in critical financial market infrastructure that interrupts the systems used to process financial transactions.

NRR26-052.text: An accidental fire or explosion at a site handling significant quantities of flammable or explosive substances.

NRR26-053.text: An accidental release of toxic gas or chemicals from a major hazard site, potentially affecting people and the surrounding environment.

NRR26-054.text: An accidental fire or explosion on an offshore oil or gas installation that handles large volumes of flammable material.

NRR26-055.text: An accidental release of flammable fuel from an onshore pipeline that leads to a fire or explosion.

NRR26-056.text: An accidental release from a major hazard pipeline carrying flammable or toxic materials, potentially causing a fire, explosion or harmful exposure.

NRR26-057.text: The accidental release of a dangerous disease-causing organism from a laboratory, potentially exposing people outside its containment arrangements.

NRR26-058.text: The collapse or breach of a dam or reservoir, suddenly releasing large volumes of fast-flowing water into surrounding areas.

NRR26-059.text: Failure of water infrastructure that leaves a large population without drinking water and may exceed the capacity for alternative supplies.

NRR26-060.text: Food contamination by disease-causing organisms, potentially leading to widespread illness and the withdrawal of affected products.

NRR26-061.text: A major fire that threatens people, property or infrastructure. It may result from accidents, deliberate acts or natural causes.

NRR26-062.text: A major interruption to data infrastructure that makes digital services unavailable across multiple organisations or sectors.

NRR26-063.text: A digital technology failure that disrupts services, potentially affecting multiple organisations or sectors at national scale.

NRR26-064.text: Accidental damage to the high-pressure national gas transmission network that interrupts its operation or the delivery of gas.

NRR26-065.text: An uncontrolled fire burning vegetation such as grass, heathland, woodland, crops or scrub, potentially threatening communities and infrastructure.

NRR26-066.text: A volcanic eruption overseas whose ash or gases could affect the UK, including disruption to air travel.

NRR26-067.text: Ground shaking caused by movement within the Earth, potentially damaging buildings and infrastructure. Damaging earthquakes are uncommon in the UK.

NRR26-068.text: A natural disaster overseas, such as an earthquake, hurricane or tsunami, that creates humanitarian needs and affects British people or interests.

NRR26-069.text: A major disaster affecting a UK Overseas Territory that requires assistance and a significant response from the UK.

NRR26-070.text: Disturbances originating from the Sun that can damage or interrupt satellites, communications, navigation and other technologies.

NRR26-071.text: A period of strong winds and storm conditions that can threaten people, damage property and disrupt transport or essential services.

NRR26-072.text: A period of unusually high temperatures, potentially harming health and placing pressure on infrastructure and essential services.

NRR26-073.text: Very cold conditions or heavy snowfall that threaten health and disrupt transport, energy supplies and other essential services.

NRR26-074.text: Flooding of coastal land caused by high tides, low-pressure weather systems, large waves or storm surges.

NRR26-075.text: Flooding when rivers, streams or brooks overflow into surrounding land, often following sustained or intense rainfall.

NRR26-076.text: Flooding when rainfall exceeds the capacity of drains and water flows across the ground. It can occur far from rivers or the coast.

NRR26-077.text: A shortage of water following an unusually dry period, potentially worsened by high demand during hot weather.

NRR26-078.text: Air pollution at levels that can damage health, including short-term episodes when weather prevents pollutants from dispersing.

NRR26-079.text: A new disease-causing organism spreading rapidly around the world where people have little existing immunity.

NRR26-080.text: An outbreak of a newly recognised infectious disease that could cause many people to become ill and require an enhanced public-health response.

NRR26-081.text: A highly infectious viral disease affecting animals including cattle, pigs, sheep, deer and goats, with serious consequences for farming.

NRR26-082.text: A severe infectious influenza disease primarily affecting birds. Prolonged direct contact can also transmit infection to some mammals, including humans.

NRR26-083.text: A viral disease spread by midges that can be fatal to horses, donkeys and mules. It does not affect humans.

NRR26-084.text: A highly contagious disease of pigs and wild boar that can spread through infected animals, meat products or contaminated objects. It does not infect humans.

NRR26-085.text: An outbreak of a plant-disease bacterium that can infect many plant species and damage agriculture or the natural environment.

NRR26-086.text: An outbreak of emerald ash borer beetles whose larvae damage ash trees, weakening them and potentially causing them to die.

NRR26-087.text: Serious disorder involving conflict or violence that can threaten public safety. It may develop from unrest or an incident that triggers wider tensions.

NRR26-088.text: Action by workers in a dispute with employers, including strikes or working to rule, that can disrupt services or infrastructure.

NRR26-089.text: A sudden return of British nationals from overseas following a crisis, creating a need for reception, accommodation and support in the UK.

NRR26-090.text: A major interruption to the operation of the criminal justice system, including pressures that prevent its core functions from continuing normally.

NRR26-091.text: Deliberate disruption of space systems or satellite services on which communications, navigation, infrastructure and defence operations depend.

NRR26-092.text: An attack on a partner country outside NATO that leads to a request for UK assistance.

NRR26-093.text: An attack on a NATO ally or qualifying deployed forces that triggers consideration of NATO’s collective-defence commitment under Article 5.

NRR26-094.text: A conventional military attack on the UK mainland or its Overseas Territories, requiring a defence and wider emergency response.

NRR26-095.text: A state misunderstanding another state’s intentions and responding with a nuclear strike, without the UK or its allies being directly involved.

flooding.text: The national register distinguishes coastal flooding, rivers overflowing their banks, and heavy rainfall overwhelming drainage. These can affect people, buildings and essential services.

weather.text: Severe weather includes storms and strong winds, unusually high temperatures, and very cold conditions or snow. These can threaten health and disrupt services.

animal-disease.text: The national register describes serious animal disease outbreaks, including foot and mouth disease, avian influenza, African horse sickness and African swine fever. Their effects differ by disease.

infectious-disease.text: Infectious disease emergencies include a new disease outbreak or a pandemic spreading internationally. They can affect many people and place pressure on health and other services.

industrial.text: Industrial emergencies include fires, explosions or toxic releases at sites and pipelines handling hazardous materials. Consequences can extend beyond the immediate facility.

transport.text: National transport scenarios include serious rail accidents, aircraft collisions and large passenger-vessel accidents, with potential casualties and major disruption.

utilities.text: Essential-service failures can interrupt electricity, gas, drinking water, communications or fuel supplies. Because these systems depend on one another, disruption can spread between services.

terrorism.text: The national register describes deliberate attacks on people, public places, transport and infrastructure. Different attack methods can cause casualties and wider disruption.

cyber.text: Cyber attacks can compromise digital systems or information and interrupt services. National scenarios cover sectors including health, transport, communications, energy, water and policing.

physical-infrastructure-attacks.text: Physical attacks on essential infrastructure can damage facilities and interrupt gas, electricity, fuel or other services.

disruption.text: National societal risks include public disorder and industrial action. They can disrupt daily activities and the delivery of essential services.

notes: Local definitions take priority. National summaries use Direct crosswalk matches; related national background is separately curated and does not change or confirm the crosswalk. Unmatched entries remain explicitly unavailable.
